description: Source-lore pass 12 imports identification systems, navigation artifacts, invention workflow, and mass-combat structure.

entries.title: Identification Practices in Kaysender
entries.summary: Nations and guilds use identity cards, craft certificates, personhood records, permits, passports, seals, and magical authentication to regulate movement, trade, work, and legal status.
body: Identification is essential wherever Kaysender's nations and trade organizations meet. Ports, borders, markets, workshops, and authorities use documents to establish identity, citizenship, profession, guild standing, and the legal right to travel or conduct business.

Merchant guilds issue cards after membership, fees, or sponsorship. These identify the holder, business affiliation, appearance, and guild seal, and may provide recognized trading rights, safe passage, fair dealing, and protection from local interference. Some guilds also monitor movement and require reports of major transactions.

Trade guilds and craft unions issue certificates recording specialty, experience, and mastery. Their cards can open restricted workshops and professional markets, guarantee standards to buyers, document skills for employment, and satisfy laws governing advanced machinery, magic, alchemy, or other dangerous work.

Governments issue citizen cards, certificates of personhood, residency and work permits, and travel passports. These documents govern property, contracts, employment, financial services, border crossing, immigration, and lawful residence.

Foreign documents may require embassy authentication or may be rejected in favor of local guilds. Because forged papers can bypass economic and legal controls, issuers use watermarks, seals, enchanted markings, wards, and magical inspection. The strictness of identification also reveals cultural values, from personal freedom to collective regulation.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Identification Practices Among Nations and Trade Guilds

entries.title: Skycompass
entries.summary: A brass-framed crystal instrument whose moving lights reveal celestial position, time, and approximate direction even when the sky is obscured.
body: A skycompass is a hand-sized polished crystal set in a circular brass frame. Flecks of light inside align with the sun, moon, and stars even through clouds, underground, or under magical obfuscation.
Sailors, merchants, explorers, and adventurers value the instrument when ordinary navigation fails. Its guidance is tied to the Material Plane and cannot distinguish between planes.

sections.heading: Legacy Mechanics Notes
body: The source allows its holder to determine time of day or night and approximate cardinal direction. This effect requires conversion.

entries.title: Tattered Trade Route Map
entries.summary: An enchanted weathered map that remembers landmarks, tracks its reader, suggests routes, and occasionally reveals hidden sites.
body: This worn parchment records a once-thriving trade route, complete with faded landmarks, favored inns, shortcuts, smudges, and personal notes. It carries the atmosphere of old journeys rather than the precision of a new chart.
The map subtly adjusts to its holder and can reveal memories of major landmarks, offer guidance through the depicted region, and expose concealed campsites or caches.

sections.heading: Legacy Mechanics Notes
body: The source requires study time, provides a Survival bonus in the depicted region, and permits a once-per-rest discovery within one mile. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Etched Skystone
entries.summary: A faintly shimmering carved stone that senses the nearest open sky and emits a brief light when struck.
body: An etched skystone is a small, smooth, dull-gray fragment carved with constellations, swirling winds, or abstract patterns. It remains cool and hums faintly in the hand.

The stone points its bearer toward the nearest open sky, making it useful in enclosed ruins, tunnels, holds, and abyssal fortifications. Tapping it against a hard surface produces a short-lived glow suitable for signaling or illumination.

sections.heading: Legacy Mechanics Notes
body: The source specifies a 10-foot light for five rounds. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Invention System
entries.summary: Kaysender inventions progress through concept, research, material gathering, crafting or enchanting, testing, improvement, and the consequences of failure.
body: The invention system supports magical items, mechanical or arcane gadgets, ship engines and hull parts, weapons, navigation systems, spells, and enchantments. Every project begins by defining what is being made and what problem it should solve.

Research establishes a viable method through experiments, experts, and study. Material gathering ties components to the invention's purpose and may create delays or force compromises when rare or suitable resources cannot be found.

Crafting or enchanting produces outcomes ranging from catastrophic failure to a revolutionary success. A working invention must then be tested in use, casting, or installation, revealing flaws, hidden benefits, or dangerous malfunctions.

Inventors can improve completed work through further research and modification. Material quality, expert assistance, magic, specialized knowledge, funding, preparation time, and temporary enchantments all affect the chance of success.

Failure is expected rather than exceptional. Minor failure wastes resources or creates flaws; major failure destroys function and forces rebuilding; critical failure can cause explosions or injury; repeated failure demands a changed approach or outside assistance.

sections.heading: Legacy Mechanics Index
body: The source supplies DC tables and modifiers for research, gathering, crafting, testing, improving, material quality, assistance, expertise, funding, time, and failure fallout. The table logic contains overlapping threshold language and must be normalized during conversion.

entries.title: Mass Combat System
entries.summary: Mass battles are shaped by direct heroic action, command decisions, logistics, magic, force strength, morale, resources, terrain, and scenario objectives.
body: Kaysender's mass-combat framework covers conflicts ranging from intimate troop skirmishes to battles involving thousands. Player characters influence these battles through direct action, command, logistical support, and magic rather than watching armies resolve in isolation.

Direct involvement includes melee and ranged attacks, offensive or defensive spellcasting, sabotage, duels with leaders, and inspiring troops. These actions can remove forces, protect allies, damage equipment, break leadership, or shift morale.

Commanders issue charges, holds, flanking maneuvers, retreats, fortification orders, dispersal, and ambushes. Each order trades position, attack power, defense, coverage, casualty risk, or surprise against the current battlefield problem.

Logistics determines whether armies can continue. Food, [[water-in-the-skies|water]], ammunition, reinforcements, medicine, repairs, rest, and entertainment affect strength, fatigue, morale, and the operation of airships or siege equipment.

Magic acts as a force multiplier through area damage, healing, enhancements, hindrances, environmental control, and summoned allies. Resolution tracks force strength, morale, resources, weather, and terrain. Victory may come through elimination, capture or sabotage of key targets, morale collapse, or completion of a specific objective.

sections.heading: Legacy Mechanics Index
body: The source provides action, order, logistics, and spell tables with attack rolls, checks, DC language, unit casualties, hit points, armor bonuses, morale modifiers, and durations. These values require a dedicated conversion and consistency pass.
